title: Vector Algebra (Addition, Component Forms, and Section Formula)
syllabus: Vectors and scalars, addition of vectors, components of a vector in two and three-dimensional space, scalar multiplication, position vector of a point, dividing a line segment in a given ratio (internal and external section formula), direction cosines and direction ratios, collinearity and coplanarity of vectors using linear combinations

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] If the position vectors of the vertices $A, B, C$ of a triangle are $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} - 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$ respectively, then the position vector of its centroid $G$ is:
questions.solution:
The centroid $\vec{g}$ of a triangle with position vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ is given by:
$$\vec{g} = \frac{\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}}{3}$$
$$\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c} = (2 + 1 + 3)\hat{i} + (-1 - 3 - 4)\hat{j} + (1 - 5 - 4)\hat{k} = 6\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} - 8\hat{k}$$
$$\vec{g} = \frac{6\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} - 8\hat{k}}{3} = 2\hat{i} - \frac{8}{3}\hat{j} - \frac{8}{3}\hat{k}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Let $P$ and $Q$ be points with position vectors $\vec{p} = 2\hat{a} + \hat{b}$ and $\vec{q} = \hat{a} - 3\hat{b}$ respectively. If a point $R$ divides the line segment $PQ$ externally in the ratio $1 : 2$, then the position vector of $R$ is:
questions.solution:
By the external section formula, the position vector of point $R$ dividing $PQ$ externally in the ratio $m : n = 1 : 2$ is:
$$\vec{r} = \frac{m\vec{q} - n\vec{p}}{m - n} = \frac{1(\hat{a} - 3\hat{b}) - 2(2\hat{a} + \hat{b})}{1 - 2}$$
$$\vec{r} = \frac{\hat{a} - 3\hat{b} - 4\hat{a} - 2\hat{b}}{-1} = \frac{-3\hat{a} - 5\hat{b}}{-1} = 3\hat{a} + 5\hat{b}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] If the vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = -4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - \lambda\hat{k}$ are collinear, then the value of $\lambda$ is:
questions.solution:
Two vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are collinear if their respective directional components are proportional:
$$\frac{a_x}{b_x} = \frac{a_y}{b_y} = \frac{a_z}{b_z}$$
$$\frac{2}{-4} = \frac{-3}{6} = \frac{4}{-\lambda}$$
$$-\frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{2} = -\frac{4}{\lambda} \implies \frac{4}{\lambda} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \lambda = 8$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A vector $\vec{r}$ is equally inclined to the coordinate axes $OX, OY,$ and $OZ$. If the magnitude of $\vec{r}$ is $6$, then the vector $\vec{r}$ can be:
questions.solution:
Let the direction cosines of $\vec{r}$ be $l, m, n$. Since it is equally inclined to the three axes:
$$l = m = n$$
Using the identity $l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1$:
$$3l^2 = 1 \implies l = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$
Thus, the unit vector along $\vec{r}$ is:
$$\hat{r} = \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})$$
Since $|\vec{r}| = 6$:
$$\vec{r} = |\vec{r}|\hat{r} = \pm 6 \left(\frac{\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \pm 2\sqrt{3}(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a triangle $ABC$, $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Then $\vec{AB} + \vec{AC}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Let $A$ be taken as the origin of reference, so the position vectors of $B$ and $C$ are $\vec{b} = \vec{AB}$ and $\vec{c} = \vec{AC}$.
Since $D$ is the midpoint of segment $BC$, its position vector is:
$$\vec{AD} = \frac{\vec{b} + \vec{c}}{2} = \frac{\vec{AB} + \vec{AC}}{2}$$
Multiplying both sides by 2:
$$\vec{AB} + \vec{AC} = 2\vec{AD}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The values of $\alpha$ for which the points with position vectors $2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$, $\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, and $7\hat{i} + \alpha\hat{j} + 15\hat{k}$ are collinear is:
questions.solution:
Let the points be $A, B, C$ with position vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$.
$$\vec{AB} = \vec{b} - \vec{a} = (1 - 2)\hat{i} + (2 - 3)\hat{j} + (3 - 5)\hat{k} = -\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$$
$$\vec{AC} = \vec{c} - \vec{a} = (7 - 2)\hat{i} + (\alpha - 3)\hat{j} + (15 - 5)\hat{k} = 5\hat{i} + (\alpha - 3)\hat{j} + 10\hat{k}$$
For the points to be collinear, $\vec{AC}$ must be parallel to $\vec{AB}$:
$$\frac{5}{-1} = \frac{\alpha - 3}{-1} = \frac{10}{-2}$$
$$-5 = -(\alpha - 3) = -5 \implies \alpha - 3 = 5 \implies \alpha = 8$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 3\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. If $\vec{c}$ is a unit vector in the direction of $2\vec{a} + \vec{b}$, then $\vec{c}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Compute the linear combination $2\vec{a} + \vec{b}$:
$$2\vec{a} + \vec{b} = 2(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}) + (3\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) = (2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 6\hat{k}) + (3\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) = 5\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$$
Magnitude of this vector:
$$|2\vec{a} + \vec{b}| = \sqrt{5^2 + 3^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{25 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}$$
Unit vector in the direction of $2\vec{a} + \vec{b}$:
$$\vec{c} = \frac{5\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}}{5\sqrt{2}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] If $O$ is the origin and $C$ is the midpoint of the line segment joining $A(2, -1, 4)$ and $B(4, 3, -2)$, then the direction cosines of $\vec{OC}$ are:
questions.solution:
Find the coordinates of the midpoint $C$:
$$C = \left(\frac{2 + 4}{2}, \frac{-1 + 3}{2}, \frac{4 + (-2)}{2}\right) = (3, 1, 1)$$
Position vector is $\vec{OC} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$.
Magnitude:
$$|\vec{OC}| = \sqrt{3^2 + 1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{9 + 1 + 1} = \sqrt{11}$$
Direction cosines $(l, m, n)$:
$$l = \frac{3}{\sqrt{11}}, \quad m = \frac{1}{\sqrt{11}}, \quad n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{11}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] If the points $A(3, 2, -4)$, $B(9, 8, -10)$, and $C(5, 4, -6)$ are collinear, the ratio in which $C$ divides the segment $AB$ internally is:
questions.solution:
Let $C$ divide $AB$ in the ratio $k : 1$.
Using the internal section formula on the x-coordinates:
$$x_C = \frac{k(x_B) + 1(x_A)}{k + 1}$$
$$5 = \frac{9k + 3}{k + 1} \implies 5(k + 1) = 9k + 3 \implies 5k + 5 = 9k + 3 \implies 4k = 2 \implies k = \frac{1}{2}$$
Checking the y-coordinate:
$$y = \frac{\frac{1}{2}(8) + 2}{\frac{1}{2} + 1} = \frac{4 + 2}{3/2} = \frac{6}{3/2} = 4$$
Checking the z-coordinate:
$$z = \frac{\frac{1}{2}(-10) - 4}{3/2} = \frac{-5 - 4}{3/2} = \frac{-9}{3/2} = -6$$
Both match point $C(5, 4, -6)$. Thus, the ratio is $1 : 2$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In a regular hexagon $ABCDEF$, if $\vec{AB} = \vec{a}$ and $\vec{BC} = \vec{b}$, then the vector $\vec{CD}$ expressed in terms of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is:
questions.solution:
In a regular hexagon $ABCDEF$, the main diagonal $\vec{AD}$ is parallel to $\vec{BC}$ and has twice its length:
$$\vec{AD} = 2\vec{BC} = 2\vec{b}$$
By vector addition along the polygon paths:
$$\vec{AD} = \vec{AB} + \vec{BC} + \vec{CD}$$
$$2\vec{b} = \vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{CD}$$
$$\vec{CD} = 2\vec{b} - \vec{b} - \vec{a} = \vec{b} - \vec{a}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Let $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ be non-coplanar vectors. If $3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b} - 5\vec{c} = x(\vec{a} - \vec{b} + \vec{c}) + y(2\vec{a} + \vec{b} - 3\vec{c})$, then the system of linear equations in $x$ and $y$ is:
questions.solution:
Since $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are linearly independent (non-coplanar), equate their respective coefficients:
For $\vec{a}$: $x + 2y = 3 \quad \text{--- (1)}$
For $\vec{b}$: $-x + y = 2 \quad \text{--- (2)}$
For $\vec{c}$: $x - 3y = -5 \quad \text{--- (3)}$
Adding (1) and (2):
$$3y = 5 \implies y = \frac{5}{3}$$
From (2): $x = y - 2 = \frac{5}{3} - 2 = -\frac{1}{3}$.
Check equation (3):
$$x - 3y = -\frac{1}{3} - 3\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{3} - 5 = -\frac{16}{3} \ne -5$$
Since equation (3) is not satisfied, the system is inconsistent and has no solution.

questions.question: If $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$, then the magnitude of the vector projection of $\vec{a} + \vec{b}$ on the z-axis is:
questions.solution:
Sum the vectors:
$$\vec{a} + \vec{b} = (2 + 1)\hat{i} + (1 + 3)\hat{j} + (-2 + 4)\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$$
The projection of any vector $\vec{v} = v_x\hat{i} + v_y\hat{j} + v_z\hat{k}$ along the z-axis is simply its z-component $|v_z|$:
$$|v_z| = 2$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] If the vectors $\vec{u} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$, $\vec{v} = \hat{i} - \hat{j}$, and $\vec{w} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ are given, and $\vec{r}$ is a vector such that $\vec{r} = x\vec{u} + y\vec{v} + z\vec{w} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$, then $x + y + z$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Express in components:
$$x(\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + y(\hat{i} - \hat{j}) + z(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$$
$$(x + y + z)\hat{i} + (x - y + 2z)\hat{j} + 3z\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}$$
Comparing the $\hat{k}$ components:
$$3z = 6 \implies z = 2$$
Comparing the $\hat{i}$ components:
$$x + y + z = 3$$
We are directly asked for the value of $x + y + z$, which equals $3$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a parallelogram $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $M$. If $O$ is any point in space, then $\vec{OA} + \vec{OB} + \vec{OC} + \vec{OD}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
In any parallelogram, the diagonals bisect each other at $M$.
Thus, $M$ is the midpoint of diagonal $AC$ and also the midpoint of diagonal $BD$.
From the midpoint property:
$$\vec{OA} + \vec{OC} = 2\vec{OM}$$
$$\vec{OB} + \vec{OD} = 2\vec{OM}$$
Adding the two relations:
$$\vec{OA} + \vec{OB} + \vec{OC} + \vec{OD} = 2\vec{OM} + 2\vec{OM} = 4\vec{OM}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The position vector of the point $R$ which divides the line joining two points $P(2\vec{a} + \vec{b})$ and $Q(\vec{a} - 2\vec{b})$ internally in the ratio $3 : 2$ is:
questions.solution:
Using the internal section formula $\vec{r} = \frac{m\vec{q} + n\vec{p}}{m + n}$ with $m = 3$ and $n = 2$:
$$\vec{r} = \frac{3(\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}) + 2(2\vec{a} + \vec{b})}{3 + 2}$$
$$\vec{r} = \frac{(3\vec{a} - 6\vec{b}) + (4\vec{a} + 2\vec{b})}{5} = \frac{7\vec{a} - 4\vec{b}}{5}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are the angles made by a directed vector $\vec{v}$ with the positive $x, y, z$ axes respectively, then the value of $\sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma$ is:
questions.solution:
The direction cosines satisfy $l = \cos\alpha, m = \cos\beta, n = \cos\gamma$, and:
$$\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1$$
Substitute $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$:
$$(1 - \sin^2\alpha) + (1 - \sin^2\beta) + (1 - \sin^2\gamma) = 1$$
$$3 - (\sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma) = 1$$
$$\sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma = 3 - 1 = 2$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] If the midpoint of the line segment joining $A(x, 2, 4)$ and $B(3, y, -2)$ is $M(1, 1, 1)$, then $(x, y)$ is:
questions.solution:
From the coordinates of the midpoint $M$:
$$\frac{x + 3}{2} = 1 \implies x + 3 = 2 \implies x = -1$$
$$\frac{2 + y}{2} = 1 \implies 2 + y = 2 \implies y = 0$$
$$\frac{4 + (-2)}{2} = \frac{2}{2} = 1 \quad \text{(verified)}$$
Thus, $(x, y) = (-1, 0)$.

questions.question: If three non-zero vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ satisfy $\vec{a} + 2\vec{b} + 3\vec{c} = \vec{0}$, then the points with position vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ are:
questions.solution:
Given the linear relation $1\vec{a} + 2\vec{b} + 3\vec{c} = \vec{0}$.
Notice that the sum of the scalar coefficients is:
$$1 + 2 + 3 = 6 \ne 0$$
However, we can rewrite it as:
$$\vec{b} = -\frac{1}{2}\vec{a} - \frac{3}{2}\vec{c}$$
Notice that $-\frac{1}{2} + \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = -2 \ne 1$.
Wait, if three points $A, B, C$ are collinear, there exist scalars $x, y, z$ not all zero such that $x\vec{a} + y\vec{b} + z\vec{c} = \vec{0}$ WITH $x + y + z = 0$.
Here $1 + 2 + 3 = 6 \ne 0$, which means $A, B, C$ and the origin $O$ are coplanar, but $A, B, C$ are not necessarily collinear.
However, if the relation is $\vec{a} - 3\vec{b} + 2\vec{c} = \vec{0}$, the sum of coefficients is $1 - 3 + 2 = 0$, which guarantees collinearity.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] If the vector $\vec{a} = x\hat{i} + (x + 1)\hat{j} + (x + 2)\hat{k}$ has a magnitude of $\sqrt{29}$, and $x > 0$, then $x$ is equal to:
[JEE Main 2020] Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be two unit vectors. If the vector $\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}$ is perpendicular to $5\vec{a} - 4\vec{b}$, then the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is:
questions.solution:
Since the two vectors are perpendicular, their scalar dot product is zero:
$$(\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}) \cdot (5\vec{a} - 4\vec{b}) = 0$$
$$5|\vec{a}|^2 - 4(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) + 10(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) - 8|\vec{b}|^2 = 0$$
$$5|\vec{a}|^2 + 6(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) - 8|\vec{b}|^2 = 0$$
Given that $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are unit vectors ($|\vec{a}| = 1, |\vec{b}| = 1$):
$$5(1) + 6(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) - 8(1) = 0$$
$$-3 + 6(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) = 0 \implies 6(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}) = 3 \implies \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = 60^\circ = \frac{\pi}{3}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] If the points $A(1, 2, 3)$, $B(4, 0, 5)$, and $C(7, -2, p)$ are collinear, find the value of $p$.
questions.solution:
Vectors along the lines:
$$\vec{AB} = (4 - 1)\hat{i} + (0 - 2)\hat{j} + (5 - 3)\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$$
$$\vec{BC} = (7 - 4)\hat{i} + (-2 - 0)\hat{j} + (p - 5)\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + (p - 5)\hat{k}$$
For collinearity, $\vec{BC} = k\vec{AB}$:
$$\frac{3}{3} = \frac{-2}{-2} = \frac{p - 5}{2}$$
$$1 = 1 = \frac{p - 5}{2} \implies p - 5 = 2 \implies p = 7.0$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the magnitude of the displacement vector from point $A(1, -2, 4)$ to point $B(4, 2, -8)$.
questions.solution:
Displacement vector is $\vec{AB} = \vec{OB} - \vec{OA}$:
$$\vec{AB} = (4 - 1)\hat{i} + (2 - (-2))\hat{j} + (-8 - 4)\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 12\hat{k}$$
Magnitude:
$$|\vec{AB}| = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2 + (-12)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13.0$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Let $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$. If a vector $\vec{r}$ satisfies $\vec{r} + 2\vec{a} = 3\vec{b}$, find the sum of the components of $\vec{r}$.
questions.solution:
Express $\vec{r}$ directly:
$$\vec{r} = 3\vec{b} - 2\vec{a}$$
$$3\vec{b} = 3(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) = 3\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + 9\hat{k}$$
$$2\vec{a} = 2(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}) = 4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$$
$$\vec{r} = (3 - 4)\hat{i} + (-6 - 6)\hat{j} + (9 - (-2))\hat{k} = -\hat{i} - 12\hat{j} + 11\hat{k}$$
Sum of the components:
$$-1 + (-12) + 11 = -13 + 11 = -2.0$$
*(Wait: $-1 - 12 + 11 = -2$. Value is $-2.0$)*

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A point $P$ divides the line segment joining $A(1, 3, 5)$ and $B(6, 8, 10)$ internally in the ratio $2 : 3$. Find the sum of the coordinates of $P$.
[JEE Main 2022] If the vector $\vec{v} = 2\hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ has a magnitude equal to $\sqrt{29}$, find the positive value of $\lambda$.
questions.solution:
Magnitude of $\vec{v}$:
$$|\vec{v}|^2 = 2^2 + \lambda^2 + 4^2 = 29$$
$$4 + \lambda^2 + 16 = 29$$
$$\lambda^2 + 20 = 29 \implies \lambda^2 = 9$$
Taking the positive value:
$$\lambda = 3.0$$
